title: Wetlands, Mangroves and Coral Reefs

cards.h: Coastal and wetland ecosystems are Prelims gold
cards.b:
Ramsar sites, Montreux Record, mangroves and coral bleaching appear in nearly every Prelims. Mains asks about coastal regulation and blue carbon.

These ecosystems protect coasts, store carbon and feed millions. They are also among the most threatened.

The Ramsar Convention (Iran, 1971; in force 1975) is the global treaty for wetlands. It promotes wise use. Sites are listed under the Ramsar List. The Montreux Record lists sites with damaged ecology. In India it includes Keoladeo and Loktak.

World Wetlands Day is 2 February. India’s Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017 replaced the 2010 rules and set a State Wetland Authority.

India’s first Ramsar sites were Chilika and Keoladeo (1981). A government summary reported 103 Ramsar sites as of October 2026, covering over 13.8 lakh hectares in 28 States and UTs (as of 2026; earlier 2026 sources show lower numbers because sites were being added).

India ranks first in Asia and third in the world by number. Tamil Nadu has the most sites. The Sundarbans is the largest Ramsar site in India by area.

Mangroves grow in the intertidal zone. Adaptations: pneumatophores (breathing roots), stilt roots, viviparity (seeds germinate on the tree) and salt excretion.

They guard against cyclones and tsunamis, nurse fish and store “blue carbon.” India has roughly 5,000 sq km of mangroves (ISFR). West Bengal (Sundarbans) has the biggest share, followed by Gujarat and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Budget 2023–24 announced MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes) and Amrit Dharohar for wetlands. Mangroves are protected in CRZ-I under the Coastal Regulation Zone rules.

The Green Credit Programme also lists mangrove restoration as an activity.

Corals are animals (polyps) with algae called zooxanthellae living inside them. They give colour and food. Reefs are fringing, barrier or atoll.

They need warm (about 23 to 29 °C), clear, shallow, saline water. They cover under 1 percent of the ocean but support about a quarter of marine species.

When water is too warm, corals expel algae and turn white: bleaching. Other threats: ocean acidification, pollution, dynamite fishing and cyclones.

The world has seen a fourth global bleaching event since 2023, the most widespread on record. India’s reef regions are the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The Coastal Regulation Zone Notification 2019 replaced the 2011 rules. CRZ-I is ecologically sensitive (mangroves, corals; with an inter-tidal part), CRZ-II is built-up urban shore, CRZ-III is rural and undeveloped, and CRZ-IV covers water area up to 12 nautical miles.

Critics argue the 2019 rules allowed more building near beaches. Supporters say they help livelihoods and give clearer zones.

Chilika (Odisha), Loktak (Manipur), Sundarbans, Bhitarkanika mangroves and Gulf of Mannar corals are key cases. Kolkata’s East Kolkata Wetlands treat the city’s sewage naturally.

Wetlands are lost to reclamation and encroachment in Bengaluru, Chennai and Srinagar, and floods in Chennai (2015) showed the cost.

Mains-style: “Why are wetlands called the kidneys of the landscape? What threats do Indian wetlands face?” Structure: functions; Ramsar and rules; threats (encroachment, sewage, invasives); remedies (wise use, community role, Amrit Dharohar).

Prelims tip: Montreux Record: Keoladeo and Loktak. First Ramsar sites: Chilika and Keoladeo. Mangroves are CRZ-I. Know the five reef areas.
